plants.name: Helianthus annuus
plants.description: A tall annual with large, daisy-like flower heads that have bright yellow ray petals around a dark central disc. The heads track the sun during early growth, and mature plants can reach 3 meters. It is widely cultivated for seeds, oil, and ornamental use.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-summer to early autumn (July to September) in the Northern Hemisphere
plants.location: Native to North America; cultivated across Europe, Russia, Ukraine, the United States, and Argentina
plants.funFact: A sunflower head is actually made up of thousands of tiny individual flowers, called florets, arranged in a spiral pattern that follows the Fibonacci sequence.

plants.name: Echinacea purpurea
plants.description: A hardy perennial prairie plant with drooping pinkish-purple petals surrounding a prominent spiky, orange-brown central cone. It is a favorite of pollinators and goldfinches, and it tolerates heat and drought well.
plants.bloomingSeason: Midsummer to early fall (June to September)
plants.location: Native to eastern and central North America; grown in gardens worldwide in temperate climates
plants.funFact: The genus name Echinacea comes from the Greek word 'echinos' meaning hedgehog, referring to the spiny central cone of the flower.

plants.name: Lavandula angustifolia
plants.description: An aromatic evergreen shrub with silvery-gray foliage and slender spikes of fragrant violet-blue flowers. By mid to late August, many lavender fields are at the tail end of peak bloom, and plants attract bees and butterflies in large numbers.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early to late summer (June to August) in the Northern Hemisphere
plants.location: Native to the Mediterranean region; widely cultivated in Provence (France), England, Bulgaria, Tasmania, and the Pacific Northwest of the United States
plants.funFact: Lavender has been used for over 2,500 years, and the name comes from the Latin 'lavare' meaning 'to wash' because the Romans used it to scent their baths.

plants.name: Acacia pycnantha
plants.description: A small Australian tree or large shrub that produces fluffy, fragrant golden-yellow globular flower clusters against sickle-shaped green leaves. Its blooming comes at the end of the southern winter, brightening the bush landscape.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to spring (July to October) in the Southern Hemisphere
plants.location: Native to southeastern Australia, including Victoria, South Australia, and New South Wales
plants.funFact: Golden Wattle is Australia's national floral emblem, and National Wattle Day is celebrated on September 1 each year to mark the start of spring.
